Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and G1415; unable, i.e. weak (literally or figuratively); passively, impossible:--could not do, impossible, impotent, not possible, weak.
BiblicalUsage: Adynatos is 'unable' or 'impossible' — the word for what human strength cannot do. The rich young ruler hears that with men salvation is impossible, but with God all things are possible; the man at Lystra was impotent in his feet, never having walked; and Hebrews says without faith it is impossible to please God. The word names our limits plainly, so that God's power can be seen clearly.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word is meant to humble me before it comforts me. Salvation is impossible with men — that is the bad news — but with God all things are possible, and that is the gospel. My inability is the very place where His power shows up.
